sections.content:
17,880 people

were counted on the census as "care escorts" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Care escorts accompany and transport adults and children between their places of residence and other destinations and act as chaperones for under 16s engaged in theatrical, television and film productions.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "care escorts" there were more women than men (81.1% compared with 18.9%).

This means "care escorts" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 18.9% and women made up 81.1% of "care escorts"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "care escorts" included:

  • houseparents and residential wardens
  • office managers
  • other administrative occupations

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "care escorts" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 60 to 64 years. Of the whole working population 6.9% were aged 60 to 64 years. For people working as "care escorts", 19% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "care escorts" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "care escorts" included:

  • caretakers
  • street cleaners
  • typists and related keyboard occupations

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "care escorts" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "care escorts" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "care escorts", 20.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (90.4% compared with 9.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (90.2%) than self-employed (9.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
